listing.name: X-COM: Terror from the Deep (OpenXcom)
listing.summary: Set up X-COM: Terror from the Deep through its upstream OpenXcom player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use your own complete unmodified original TFTD/TFD data folders. Copy the original subfolders into OpenXcom’s TFTD subdirectory, keeping their hierarchy. UFO/XCOM files do not supply this game. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: Use the official upstream download/setup route or a complete already prepared OpenXcom player, keeping its common data and standard mod resources. No GitHub release package was observed. Choose a build that documents TFTD support; an old UFO-only release is insufficient. Complete original-data and game selection through upstream before saving the player entry. Register openxcom.exe with its installation folder as working directory, retaining the upstream game selection rather than inventing a fixed argument. The upstream Windows installer may copy a detected Steam original when you deliberately run it.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Windows normally uses the actual Documents/OpenXcom user/config location; an installation-local user folder and explicit -data/-user/-config choices can change the searched locations. Preserve every actual selected data/user/config folder, including UFO/TFTD resources, mods, savegames and screenshots. Keep the two original games and their campaigns distinct even if they share one player/profile. Back up with OpenXcom closed before changing runtime or mods.

steps.title: Keep external ownership and deliberate Play
steps.instruction: Finish upstream setup first. Registration saves your selected executable, working directory and literal arguments; Play is a separate explicit action. You and upstream own this external runtime, original files and profile. Registration-only removal preserves them. Managed Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for these external files. Preserve a working copy and its data before upstream replacement. Other platforms require their own supported upstream application/native flow.
